# JSON

Build JSON objects and arrays, read values out of them, and query or transform them.

**Library:** [Standard library](index.md#standard-library), for apps and code-pipeline hooks. More in [Cogniscript](../../../concepts/cogniscript.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`JsonArrayAdd`](#jsonarrayadd) | Adds a value to the end of a JSON array and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonArrayCount`](#jsonarraycount) | Returns the number of items in a JSON array. |
| [`JsonArrayCreate`](#jsonarraycreate) | Returns a new, empty JSON array: `[]`. |
| [`JsonArrayGetAtIndex`](#jsonarraygetatindex) | Returns the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0. |
| [`JsonArrayInsert`](#jsonarrayinsert) | Inserts a JSON value into an array, before the item at a position, and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonArrayRemoveAtIndex`](#jsonarrayremoveatindex) | Removes the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonArraySetAtIndex`](#jsonarraysetatindex) | Replaces the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonAtaTransform`](#jsonatatransform) | Evaluates a JSONata expression against JSON and returns the result as JSON text. |
| [`JsonIsParseable`](#jsonisparseable) | Whether text is valid JSON of any kind: an object, an array, a string in quotes, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`. |
| [`JsonObjectCreate`](#jsonobjectcreate) | Returns a new, empty JSON object: `{}`. |
| [`JsonObjectGet`](#jsonobjectget) | Returns the value of a key in a JSON object, or empty text when the object has no such key. |
| [`JsonObjectSetBool`](#jsonobjectsetbool) | Sets a key in a JSON object to `true` or `false`, and returns the new object. |
| [`JsonObjectSetString`](#jsonobjectsetstring) | Sets a key in a JSON object to a string, and returns the new object. |
| [`JsonPathQuery`](#jsonpathquery) | Runs a JSONPath query against a JSON object and returns what it selects, as JSON text. |
| [`JsonUnescapeString`](#jsonunescapestring) | Reads a JSON string, quotes and all, and returns the text inside it with its escapes resolved. |

### JsonArrayAdd

Adds a value to the end of a JSON array and returns the new array.

```c
jsonArray JsonArrayAdd(jsonArray array, string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The array to add to. An empty value counts as an empty array. |
| `value` | `string` | The value to add: JSON text (an object, an array, a number, `true`, `false`, `null` or a string in quotes) is added as that JSON, and any other text as a string. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The new array, as JSON text.

The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back: `items = JsonArrayAdd(items, value);`.

Text that is valid JSON is added as that JSON, so text that only looks like JSON changes kind: `42` is added as a number, `true` as a bool and `null` as JSON `null`. To add such text as a string, pass it as a JSON string, in quotes: `"\"42\""`. All other text, a guid for example, is added as a string.

### JsonArrayCount

Returns the number of items in a JSON array.

```c
int JsonArrayCount(jsonArray array)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The array to count. |

**Returns** `int`: The number of items.

An empty value counts as an empty array and gives 0, so counting a key that [`JsonObjectGet`](#jsonobjectget) did not find gives 0 rather than an error. Raises an error when the value is not a JSON array, such as an object.

### JsonArrayCreate

Returns a new, empty JSON array: `[]`.

```c
jsonArray JsonArrayCreate()
```

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The text `[]`.

### JsonArrayGetAtIndex

Returns the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0.

```c
string JsonArrayGetAtIndex(jsonArray array, int index)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The array to read. |
| `index` | `int` | The position of the item, from 0 to one less than the count. |

**Returns** `string`: The item, as text.

A string item comes back as its text, without quotes. A number, `true` or `false` comes back as written. An object or an array comes back as indented JSON text, ready to store in a `jsonObject` or a `jsonArray`. A `null` item comes back as empty text.

Raises `Index 5 is out of range for length 2` when the index is past the last item. A negative index raises an error too.

### JsonArrayInsert

Inserts a JSON value into an array, before the item at a position, and returns the new array.

```c
jsonArray JsonArrayInsert(jsonArray array, int index, string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The array to insert into. |
| `index` | `int` | The position of the item to insert before, from 0 to one less than the count. |
| `value` | `string` | The value to insert, as JSON: an object, an array, a number, `true`, `false`, `null`, or a string in quotes. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The new array, as JSON text.

The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back.

Unlike [`JsonArrayAdd`](#jsonarrayadd), the value must be JSON: plain text such as `hello` raises `Error parsing value to JSON: …`, so pass a string in quotes, `"\"hello\""`.

The index must point at an existing item, so this call cannot insert at the end of an array or into an empty one; use [`JsonArrayAdd`](#jsonarrayadd) for those. An index past the last item raises `Index 2 is out of range for length 2`, and a negative index raises an error too.

### JsonArrayRemoveAtIndex

Removes the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array.

```c
jsonArray JsonArrayRemoveAtIndex(jsonArray array, int index)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The array to remove from. |
| `index` | `int` | The position of the item to remove, from 0 to one less than the count. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The new array, as JSON text.

The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back. Raises `Index 5 is out of range for length 2` when the index is past the last item, and an error for a negative index.

### JsonArraySetAtIndex

Replaces the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array.

```c
jsonArray JsonArraySetAtIndex(jsonArray array, int index, string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The array to change. |
| `index` | `int` | The position of the item to replace, from 0 to one less than the count. |
| `value` | `string` | The new value, as JSON: an object, an array, a number, `true`, `false`, `null`, or a string in quotes. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The new array, as JSON text.

The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back.

Unlike [`JsonArrayAdd`](#jsonarrayadd), the value must be JSON: plain text such as `hello` raises `Error parsing value to JSON: …`, so pass a string in quotes, `"\"hello\""`. An index past the last item raises `Index 5 is out of range for length 2`, and a negative index raises an error too.

### JsonAtaTransform

Evaluates a JSONata expression against JSON and returns the result as JSON text.

```c
string JsonAtaTransform(string value, string transform)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The JSON to evaluate the expression against: an object, an array or any other JSON value. |
| `transform` | `string` | The JSONata expression. |

**Returns** `string`: The result as JSON text, or empty text when the expression matches nothing.

JSONata is a query and transformation language for JSON (see jsonata.org). Use it to pick values out (`customer.name`), collect them (`[items.price]` gives an array of every price), compute (`$sum(items.price)`) or build new JSON (`{ 'name': customer.name, 'total': $sum(items.price) }`). Without the square brackets, `items.price` gives an array only when there are several prices; for one item it gives that single value.

It is also how to store a number, an array or a nested object under a key, which [`JsonObjectSetString`](#jsonobjectsetstring) cannot do: `JsonAtaTransform(order, "$merge([$, {'count': 3}])")` returns `order` with `count` set to the number 3.

The result is JSON, so a string result keeps its quotes: `"Ada"`, not `Ada`. Pass it to [`JsonUnescapeString`](#jsonunescapestring) for the bare text. An object or an array comes back as indented JSON. When the expression matches nothing the result is empty text.

Raises `Failed to perform JSONPath query: …` when the expression is invalid or the value is not JSON. The message says JSONPath, but the detail after it is about the JSONata expression or the JSON.

### JsonIsParseable

Whether text is valid JSON of any kind: an object, an array, a string in quotes, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`.

```c
bool JsonIsParseable(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to check. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when `value` is valid JSON.

Empty text is not JSON, and neither is a plain word such as `hello`: a JSON string needs its quotes. To check for an object or an array, use [`TypeIsJsonObject`](type-checks.md#typeisjsonobject) or [`TypeIsJsonArray`](type-checks.md#typeisjsonarray). [`TypeIsJson`](type-checks.md#typeisjson) is the same check except that it says `false` for `null`.

### JsonObjectCreate

Returns a new, empty JSON object: `{}`.

```c
jsonObject JsonObjectCreate()
```

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The text `{}`.

### JsonObjectGet

Returns the value of a key in a JSON object, or empty text when the object has no such key.

```c
string JsonObjectGet(jsonObject obj, string key)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `obj` | `jsonObject` | The object to read. |
| `key` | `string` | The key, matched exactly, including case. |

**Returns** `string`: The value, as text, or empty text when the key is missing or its value is `null`.

A string value comes back as its text, without quotes. A number, `true` or `false` comes back as written (`1.50` stays `1.50`). An object or an array comes back as indented JSON text, ready to store in a `jsonObject` or a `jsonArray`. A missing key and a `null` value both give empty text, so test for them with [`StringIsEmpty`](strings.md#stringisempty) or by comparing with `""`; [`TypeIsNull`](type-checks.md#typeisnull) does not detect them.

To read a nested value, read one level at a time: `JsonObjectGet(JsonObjectGet(order, "customer"), "name")`. Raises an error when `obj` is empty or not a JSON object, so check that a nested object is there before reading inside it. A missing array is safe: passed to a call that takes a `jsonArray`, such as [`JsonArrayCount`](#jsonarraycount), empty text counts as an empty array.

### JsonObjectSetBool

Sets a key in a JSON object to `true` or `false`, and returns the new object.

```c
jsonObject JsonObjectSetBool(jsonObject obj, string key, bool value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `obj` | `jsonObject` | The object to change. |
| `key` | `string` | The key to set, matched exactly, including case. It is added when it is missing. |
| `value` | `bool`, can be empty | The value to store under `key`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The new object, as compact JSON text.

Adds the key when it is missing and replaces its value when it is there. The object you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back: `result = JsonObjectSetBool(result, "done", true);`. The value is stored as a JSON bool, not as text. Empty text is stored as `false`; other text that is not `true` or `false`, such as `yes`, raises an error.

### JsonObjectSetString

Sets a key in a JSON object to a string, and returns the new object.

```c
jsonObject JsonObjectSetString(jsonObject obj, string key, string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `obj` | `jsonObject` | The object to change. |
| `key` | `string` | The key to set, matched exactly, including case. It is added when it is missing. |
| `value` | `string`, can be empty | The value to store under `key`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The new object, as compact JSON text.

Adds the key when it is missing and replaces its value when it is there. The object you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back: `result = JsonObjectSetString(result, "name", name);`.

The value is always stored as a JSON string, even when it is a number or JSON text: `JsonObjectSetString(o, "count", "3")` gives `{"count":"3"}`, and an object you pass in is stored as a string of JSON text. To store a number, an array or a nested object, use [`JsonAtaTransform`](#jsonatatransform), for example [`JsonAtaTransform(o, "$merge([$, {'count': 3}])")`](#jsonatatransform).

### JsonPathQuery

Runs a JSONPath query against a JSON object and returns what it selects, as JSON text.

```c
string JsonPathQuery(string value, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The JSON object to query, as text. |
| `path` | `string` | The JSONPath, starting at `$`. |

**Returns** `string`: What the path selects, as JSON text, or empty text when it selects nothing.

Paths start at `$`: `$.customer.name`, `$.items[0]`, `$.items[*].price`, or a filter such as `$.items[?(@.price > 10)].name`. The value queried must be a JSON object; an array at the top level raises an error.

One match comes back as indented JSON, so a string keeps its quotes: `"Ada"`, not `Ada`. Pass it to [`JsonUnescapeString`](#jsonunescapestring) for the bare text. No match gives empty text.

Several matches come back between square brackets, one per line, each followed by a comma. The comma after the last one makes that text invalid JSON, so [`StringToJsonArray`](conversion.md#stringtojsonarray) and [`TypeIsJsonArray`](type-checks.md#typeisjsonarray) reject it. To collect several values as an array, use [`JsonAtaTransform`](#jsonatatransform) instead: `[items.price]` there gives an array of every price, however many there are.

Raises `Failed to perform JSONPath query: …` when the value is not a JSON object or the path is invalid.

### JsonUnescapeString

Reads a JSON string, quotes and all, and returns the text inside it with its escapes resolved.

```c
string JsonUnescapeString(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string`, can be empty | The JSON string, including its double quotes. |

**Returns** `string`: The text inside the quotes.

Use it on a string result from [`JsonPathQuery`](#jsonpathquery) or [`JsonAtaTransform`](#jsonatatransform): it turns `"Ada"` into `Ada`, and escapes such as `\n`, `\"` and `é` into the characters they stand for.

A bare number, `true` or `false` comes back as it is, and empty text or `null` gives empty text. Other text without quotes raises `Failed to unescape string: …`. For text that has backslash escapes but no surrounding quotes, use [`StringUnescape`](strings.md#stringunescape).
